factors.factor: Mismatch between the IPC Template Type definition (expecting 21 inputs) and the sensor code supplying only 20 input values, a defect that was never reconciled.
factors.evidence: "The definition of the IPC Template Type in the Template Type Definitions file stated that it expected 21 input fields. The sensor code that invoked the Content Interpreter with Channel File 291's Template Instances supplied only 20 input values to match against."

factors.factor: Testing was focused on functional validation and did not exercise the 21st input field with realistic or non-wildcard criteria, so the mismatch went undetected.
factors.evidence: "Manual and automated testing were performed during development, focused on functional validation"; "a static set of 12 test cases was selected... used a regex wildcard matching criterion in the 21st field for all Template Instances."

factors.factor: The stress test used a single test Template Instance and passed, giving false confidence in the Template Type's robustness.
factors.evidence: "The IPC Template Type was stress tested with a test Template Instance... It passed the stress test and was validated for use."

factors.factor: The Content Validator checked channel files against the expected 21-input definition rather than against what the sensor code actually supplies, so it passed content that would crash sensors.
factors.evidence: "The Content Validator evaluated the new Template Instances. It based its assessment on the expectation that the IPC Template Type would be provided with 21 inputs."

factors.factor: The 21st input field had never been used by any previously deployed Template Instance, so the new non-wildcard criterion exercised an untested code path in production.
factors.evidence: "No IPC Template Instances in previous channel file versions had used the 21st input parameter field."

factors.factor: Rapid Response Content was deployed to the full sensor fleet without staged rollout or canarying, so a faulty content update reached all affected systems at once.
factors.evidence: "The new Template Instances were sent to sensors." (deployed in a single content update on July 19, with recovery measured fleet-wide on July 29)

factors.factor: Memory-safety weakness in the kernel-mode sensor: the code performed a NULL check but then read through an invalid pointer, and the kernel driver ran in a context where a fault crashes the whole system.
factors.evidence: "The code read the input at index 0x14 (the 21st element), which did not point to valid memory. The code performed a NULL pointer check, then read through the invalid pointer, resulting in the out-of-bounds read and the bugcheck."

factors.factor: Configuration data (Rapid Response Content) was treated as lower-risk than code, so it bypassed the kernel-level safety scrutiny applied to sensor releases, and the sensor's content interpreter was not defended against malformed input arity.
factors.evidence: "Rapid Response Content is configuration data; it is not code or a kernel driver."
